red.focus: Organize evidence so someone else can check what it proves.
red.summary: A case file becomes useful when documents, witnesses, dates, and disputes can be found and verified. Learn to keep original material safe, label it accurately, and connect each item to a legal question.
checklist: I can create a dated evidence inventory
I can separate an item's contents from its reliability
I can identify a safe next preservation step

sections.title: Start with a timeline and original sources
sections.body_md: A customer says that a refrigerator caught fire three weeks after installation. Gather purchase records, installation messages, photographs, fire reports, and relevant witness names. Note the time each source was created and when it was obtained. The claim that the fire began inside the appliance should remain marked as an allegation until evidence supports it. Do not merge the client's later recollection into a report as though it were recorded on the day. A simple table with date, source, custodian, and disputed fact helps the lawyer see what can actually be tested.

sections.title: Keep originals and trace copies
sections.body_md: A phone photograph can be copied for review, but preserve the original file when possible, including available metadata, and record how the copy was made. Changing its caption to describe an unproved cause creates confusion. A witnessed email may authenticate one communication without proving everything alleged in its text. Store confidential records with appropriate safeguards and avoid sending them to unauthorized people. The correct handling of physical objects and digital devices depends on law and policy. Evidence organization should enable reliable examination, not create an appearance of certainty.

sections.title: Connect the item to a proposition
sections.body_md: The installation invoice may show a transaction; a timestamped message might show notice of a malfunction; an expert's analysis may bear on the cause of a fire. None necessarily proves that the seller was legally negligent. Link each item to the issue it addresses, and record contrary evidence too. Ask whether there are missing inspection records or alternative causes. A useful evidence table tells the next reader what the item is, how its authenticity might be shown, which fact it supports, and which question it leaves open.

yellow.focus: Build an admissibility-aware evidence chart distinguishing relevance and reliability.
yellow.summary: Relevance is not the same as admissibility, and an authenticated record need not be true. Create a proposition-by-proposition exhibit plan with source, objections, and missing foundations.
checklist: I can connect each element to supporting and adverse evidence
I can distinguish relevance, authentication and hearsay concerns
I can identify gaps without hiding unfavorable material

sections.title: List what the tribunal must decide
sections.body_md: A plaintiff claims that defective wiring caused a house fire. Make a separate row for duty, breach, causation, and the claimed loss under the relevant law. Link each row to photographs, inspection records, witness accounts, and expert opinions, including items that challenge the theory. Relevance asks whether an item has a tendency to affect a fact of consequence under the applicable evidence law; it is only the first question. A recording that appears helpful may still face rules about authentication, hearsay, privilege, or exclusion for unfair prejudice.

sections.title: Different evidence rules answer different questions
sections.body_md: In U.S. federal proceedings, Federal Rules of Evidence 401 and 402 address relevance and general admissibility of relevant evidence; Rule 403 permits exclusion in specified circumstances despite relevance. Rule 901 concerns sufficient proof that an item is what its proponent claims, with some self-authenticating categories in Rule 902. Jurisdictions and tribunals differ. An authentic email proves that a communication exists or occurred, not necessarily the truth of every factual assertion within it. A legal evidence chart should record these distinctions rather than label an exhibit 'admissible' solely because it looks genuine.

sections.title: Record objections and lawful solutions
sections.body_md: A hearsay problem may require a witness with personal knowledge, an applicable exception, or different proof. Confidential material may be privileged or subject to protective rules. Do not solve admissibility by changing a statement or concealing an unfavorable report. Note the foundation still needed, the strongest expected objection, and lawful alternatives. A practical chart can include columns for proposition, exhibit, witness, provenance, relevance, potential objection, and response. The lawyer should then check local procedural and evidence rules instead of relying on a generic template to make final admission decisions.

orange.focus: Structure a digital evidence record with provenance and defensible forensic limits.
orange.summary: Electronic records can be altered, duplicated, or taken out of context. Design a proportionate collection protocol and evidentiary narrative that separates authenticity, integrity, meaning, and admissibility.
checklist: I can explain why a hash verifies integrity without proving truth
I can distinguish metadata from an inferred human action
I can build a reproducible, privacy-respecting collection process

sections.title: Digital provenance has several layers
sections.body_md: A cloud log records that a user account accessed a confidential file at 03:12. The record may be genuine, but it does not necessarily prove which human controlled the account. Device sharing, time-zone settings, automation, and credential theft can change the inference. Verify the log source, clock configuration, retention settings, and who exported it. A cryptographic hash can help show that a copy has not changed since it was hashed, but it cannot prove that the underlying record was accurate when created. Treat source integrity, attribution, and substantive meaning as distinct propositions.

A cryptographic hash can help show that a copy has not changed since it was hashed, but it cannot prove that the underlying record was accurate when created. Treat source integrity, attribution, and substantive meaning as distinct propositions.

sections.title: Collect what law permits and what the case needs
sections.body_md: A preservation request may cover relevant emails and audit logs, but wholesale collection of unrelated private messages may be disproportionate or unlawful. Define scope using custodian, time range, topic, and identified systems. Record collection tools and steps, permissions, chain of custody, and any processing that changed the file format. Respect privilege, privacy and disclosure duties. An expert may need to explain the limitations of automated extraction and any missing data. A reproducible workflow makes defense challenges possible rather than trying to defeat them through obscurity.

sections.title: Translate technical records into legal proof
sections.body_md: A timeline might show when a contract was signed, when access permissions changed, and when a disputed transfer occurred. Each event should link to an authenticated source and distinguish documented fact from an expert's inference. Identify competing explanations, such as a scheduled backup operation. Then apply the correct legal test for breach, intent, causation, or confidentiality, without presuming that technical anomalies prove a crime. A master's advocate should be able to explain the evidence accurately to someone unfamiliar with the technology and identify what further examination would reasonably change the conclusion.

black.focus: Design an evidence architecture robust against uncertainty, bias, and institutional inequality.
black.summary: Decisions increasingly rely on complex records, scientific inference, and automated classification. Construct an evidentiary system that exposes error sources, protects legitimate privacy, and lets opposing parties meaningfully test proof.
checklist: I can separate authenticity, admissibility, probative weight and sufficiency
I can evaluate model error and selection effects in a legal record
I can defend a rights-respecting approach to disclosure and expert review

sections.title: Organize proof as an auditable argument
sections.body_md: An agency relies on algorithmic fraud scores to deny hundreds of benefits. A chart of scores alone does not reveal training-data bias, false-positive rates, missing variables, or whether individual facts satisfy the governing statutory standard. Trace each evidence item to its source, method of creation, validation, and the precise proposition it supports. Separate whether the tribunal may consider the item from how much weight it deserves. The issue is not whether statistical information has legal value, but whether affected people can understand and challenge the inference used against them.

The issue is not whether statistical information has legal value, but whether affected people can understand and challenge the inference used against them.

sections.title: Selection and missingness are substantive problems
sections.body_md: A dataset might contain only people previously investigated, so its observed relationship between behavior and wrongdoing may reflect enforcement patterns. Missing records may be systematic, not random. Distinguish observed correlation from causal inference and avoid imputing guilt from demographic proxies. A serious evidence plan considers expert competence, reproducibility, access to source materials under lawful protections, and alternatives if sensitive data cannot be publicly disclosed. The legal system must balance challenge rights, privacy, proprietary interests, and security without making any of them an automatic trump card.

sections.title: Make the record contestable and humane
sections.body_md: Build a layered record: authenticated source materials, transparent methods, independent validation, competing hypotheses, and a map from evidence to legally required elements. Protect privileged or confidential information through lawful procedures, not concealment. Provide meaningful opportunities to correct erroneous data and explain what an unfavorable finding would require. Consider resource asymmetries between the agency and the person denied essential support. A doctoral evidence architecture is successful when it permits rigorous disagreement and reduces unjustified coercion, not merely when it produces a polished exhibit binder.
